subject: deciding whether to spend GitHub Copilot's metered budget on a task vs a cheaper or free lane
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Concept, Coverage, Philosophy, the routing-decision table, the cost-model-and-plan-allowances table, Strengths and weaknesses, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and references/model-facts.md.

cases.scenario: A developer is running every routine task — reformatting files, renaming variables across a few files, generating obvious boilerplate — through Copilot's metered chat/agent surface, and is surprised their monthly premium allowance is nearly exhausted by mid-cycle.
cases.context: The work is low-complexity and largely mechanical. The account is on a plan with a finite monthly allowance and no rollover.
cases.question: Why is the allowance draining, and how should the agent change the routing?
expected_flags: Low-complexity, mechanical work is being spent on the finite metered surface — that is the core waste this routing discipline prevents
Boilerplate, formatting, and repetitive transformations should go to a free/cheap lane or a deterministic script, not the metered surface
The allowance is finite and non-rolling, so wasted metered requests are gone at cycle end
expected_fix_hints: Route boilerplate/formatting/mechanical edits to a script or a free model lane
Reserve the metered surface for work an IDE-native frontier model genuinely earns
absent_signals: Do not recommend keeping mechanical work on the metered surface
Do not claim the metered allowance is effectively unlimited because a subscription is paid

cases.scenario: A team lead asserts that since everyone has a paid Copilot subscription, running large multi-file agentic refactors through Copilot 'costs nothing extra,' and plans to move all agent flows there.
cases.context: Agent flows are multi-file and token-heavy. The plan has a capped metered allowance.
cases.question: Is that assertion correct, and how should the agent respond?
expected_flags: A paid subscription does not make metered agent flows free — it buys unmetered completions plus a capped, non-rolling metered allowance
Agentic multi-file flows burn the metered allowance fastest of all
Cost is token-based at a per-model rate (AI credits, 1 credit = $0.01), not zero and not a flat per-request charge
expected_fix_hints: Treat agent flows as the most expensive metered use and route only the ones that genuinely earn it through Copilot
Estimate cost token-based (input + output + cached x per-model rate), not as 'free because subscribed'
absent_signals: Do not affirm that a subscription makes metered agent flows free
Do not assume unlimited usage from the subscription

cases.scenario: A developer asks whether they should ration their inline code completions and next-edit suggestions to preserve their premium allowance for the rest of the month.
cases.context: The question is specifically about the inline completion / next-edit surface, not chat or agent flows.
cases.question: Do completions consume the metered allowance, and what should the agent advise?
expected_flags: Inline completions and next-edit suggestions are the always-free, unmetered surface — they are not billed in the metered allowance
There is no budgeting decision to make for the free completion surface; it is the cheapest, strongest value
Only the chat/agent surface draws from the finite metered allowance

Budget only the metered chat/agent surface
absent_signals: Do not claim inline completions consume the premium/credit allowance
Do not advise rationing the always-free surface

cases.scenario: An engineer estimates Copilot cost for a current-month task using the old per-model premium-request multipliers (e.g. '1x for the premium model, 13x for code review') and concludes the task is cheap.
cases.context: The account is on the current usage-based billing introduced June 1 2026, not a legacy annual plan.
cases.question: Is that cost estimate using the right model, and how should the agent correct it?
expected_flags: Post-June-1-2026 billing is token-based AI credits (1 credit = $0.01), computed from input + output + cached tokens x a per-model rate
The per-model premium-request multipliers were retired by the usage-based shift and should not be used for a current-month estimate
Cost reasoning must use the current model unless the account is explicitly on legacy annual billing
expected_fix_hints: Re-estimate cost using token-based AI credits at the model's per-token rate
Confirm whether the account is on the current usage-based model or a legacy annual plan before estimating
absent_signals: Do not use the retired per-request multipliers for a current usage-based account
Do not present the multiplier-based estimate as the current cost model

cases.scenario: A developer wants frontier-model help reasoning through a tricky refactor that depends heavily on context the editor already has open (the current file, its imports, the diagnostics), and asks whether this is a good use of Copilot's metered surface.
cases.context: The task genuinely benefits from in-editor context and a frontier model; it is not mechanical or high-volume.
cases.question: Is the metered surface the right place for this, and why?
expected_flags: Genuine IDE-native frontier chat/refactor that needs context the editor already has is exactly what the metered allowance is for
This is the work that earns the metered spend — the in-editor flow and existing context are the value
It is not mechanical or high-volume, so routing it off to a script/free lane would lose the IDE-native benefit
expected_fix_hints: Spend metered Copilot budget here — the IDE-native frontier flow earns it
Keep mechanical/high-volume work off the metered surface, but not this
absent_signals: Do not route genuine IDE-native frontier work off Copilot purely to save credits
Do not treat every metered use as waste

cases.scenario: A team has already decided to move a bulk classification job off Copilot to a free open-weight model lane, and now asks which specific free model to pick for the job and how to invoke the OpenCode CLI non-interactively for it.
cases.context: The Copilot spend decision is already made (off Copilot). The remaining questions are free-model choice and runtime invocation.
cases.question: How should the agent scope this request?
expected_flags: Picking a specific free model is owned by a different skill (opencode-free-models), not Copilot routing
Invoking/operating the OpenCode runtime is owned by the opencode skill, not this one
The Copilot spend decision is already settled; the open questions sit outside this skill's lane
expected_fix_hints: Route the free-model selection to opencode-free-models
Route the OpenCode CLI invocation question to the opencode skill
absent_signals: Do not recommend a specific free model as if Copilot routing owned that choice
Do not answer the OpenCode runtime/CLI question as part of Copilot spend routing
